# n1 - The roadmap graph model

`RoadmapGraph.analyze(roadmap_path, index_path:)` reads one roadmap file into the same shape the
node scope already uses: entries with their INDEX-reconciled status, the edge map from
`## Graph`, the cycle path when one exists, the topological batches, the critical paths, and the
ready set. Edges are parsed by `GraphEdges`; batches, critical paths, and downstream hops come
from `ReadySet`. This node writes no file and reads no clock.

## n1 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.1 | Parse `## Graph` through `GraphEdges.parse` | A local edge regex here means the roadmap scope and the node scope can disagree about what an edge is, which is the exact drift 327 C1 forbids | `roadmap_graph_test#test_edges_come_from_graph_edges_not_a_local_parser` |
| 1.2 | Detect a cycle at read and return the whole path | A cyclic roadmap yields an invented topological order, and the reader dispatches work in an order nobody chose | `roadmap_graph_test#test_cyclic_graph_returns_whole_cycle_path_and_no_batches` |
| 1.3 | Compute batches through `ReadySet.batches` | A second topological sort here drifts from the node scope, so the same edge set produces two different batch numbers depending on who asks | `roadmap_graph_test#test_batches_match_ready_set_batches_for_the_same_edges` |
| 1.4 | Compute the critical path through `ReadySet.critical_paths` | The hop count is computed locally and disagrees with the node scope, so the long pole a reader is shown is not the long pole the ranker uses | `roadmap_graph_test#test_critical_paths_match_ready_set_for_the_same_edges` |
| 1.5 | Reconcile each entry's status against INDEX.md, INDEX winning | A stale checkbox in the roadmap file marks an entry delivered, the ready set opens the work that entry blocks, and an executor starts on an unmet dependency | `roadmap_graph_test#test_index_status_wins_over_the_roadmap_checkbox` |
| 1.6 | Meld in an entry the graph does not name as needing nothing | A partly migrated roadmap silently drops every entry the graph has not learned yet, so real work disappears from the batches | `roadmap_graph_test#test_entry_absent_from_graph_is_merged_in_as_a_root` |
| 1.7 | Report an id the graph names that no batch lists | The model invents an entry with no title and no status, or raises, on a roadmap whose graph ran ahead of its batch list | `roadmap_graph_test#test_graph_id_with_no_batch_entry_is_reported_not_invented` |
| 1.8 | Handle a roadmap with no `## Graph` section | The model raises and every caller, including the screens, dies on the twenty-one live roadmaps that have no graph yet | `roadmap_graph_test#test_roadmap_without_graph_returns_named_reason_not_raise` |
| 1.9 | Handle a roadmap with neither `## Batches` nor `## Waves` | `RoadmapSavepoint::MissingGroupingHeading` escapes the model and takes down the caller instead of being reported | `roadmap_graph_test#test_missing_grouping_heading_is_an_error_not_an_exception` |
| 1.10 | Count a need as met only when it is delivered | An abandoned or blocked need is counted as met, and the ready set opens work whose dependency will never land | `roadmap_graph_test#test_abandoned_need_does_not_make_an_entry_ready` |
| 1.11 | Ignore edge lines inside a fenced block | A fenced example in the roadmap prose is read as a real edge, and a documentation snippet reorders the delivery | `roadmap_graph_test#test_fenced_example_edges_are_not_read_as_real` |
| 1.12 | Match the `## Graph` heading exactly | A heading such as `## Graph (superseded 2026-09-01)` is matched as a prefix and a retired section drives the live order | `roadmap_graph_test#test_graph_heading_matches_exactly_not_by_prefix` |
| 1.13 | Survive an invalid UTF-8 byte in the roadmap file | `ArgumentError: invalid byte sequence` takes down the model, the screens, and `roadmap-next` on one bad byte | `roadmap_graph_test#test_invalid_utf8_byte_does_not_raise` |
| 1.14 | Keep the model free of a clock and an environment seam | The model reads `Time.now` or an env var and becomes untestable and unreproducible. Melded at review (A11): this is a hermeticity guard, not a determinism proof, and the source scan is stated as such so the close gate never reads it as one; determinism itself is proven by row 2.4 | `roadmap_graph_test#test_library_source_reads_no_clock_or_environment` |
| 1.15 | Report a dead-end need rather than silently blocking behind it | Melded at review (A10, D15): an abandoned entry in an early batch blocks every entry behind it forever, `state` goes `exhausted`, the auto loop stops, and nothing in the payload says why. `ReadySet.dead_end?` already answers this at node scope | `roadmap_graph_test#test_need_on_an_abandoned_entry_is_reported_as_a_dead_end` |
| 1.16 | Keep the roadmap file order of entries within a batch | Melded at review (A8, D11): `ReadySet.batches` sorts each layer lexically, which on one live roadmap flips the auto loop rank 1 from `5` to `2`. A computed batch must not quietly become a ranking decision; only the injected ranker may reorder | `roadmap_graph_test#test_entries_within_a_batch_keep_roadmap_file_order` |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code in this node.
2. Write the code that makes them pass.
3. Green, then `ruby bin/test` at its baseline before the next node starts.
